title: Tier C — no mechanical oracle (human judgment)

ontology.definition: a new user completing the core action within 24 hours of signup

objective.claim: Onboarding change X raises 24-hour activation without harming week-4 retention.

success.successCriterion: A change design with an argued causal mechanism and a measurement plan that a human reviewer judges credible.
nonGoals: A change that raises activation via dark patterns that then hurt retention.
A plausible-sounding rationale with no measurement plan attached.

approaches.name: friction-removal
approaches.lens: cut steps before the core action

approaches.name: motivation
approaches.lens: raise perceived value at first run

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: activation up but retention down (a dark pattern)
adversarialChecklist.check: require a week-4 retention guardrail metric alongside activation

adversarialChecklist.failureMode: novelty effect mistaken for durable lift
adversarialChecklist.check: require a 4-week holdout read, not a 1-week read

verifier.ceiling: There is no mechanical check here: no run establishes the causal claim. Every conclusion rests on human judgment and must be labeled UNVERIFIED. The adversarial checklist reduces obvious errors but cannot confirm the change works.

tripwires.observation: 24-hour activation rate for the treatment cohort vs control
tripwires.whatWouldFalsify: in an adequately powered A/B test (sized for 80% power to detect the pre-registered minimum meaningful effect of +2pp activation), the treatment's 24h activation lift is at or below 0. An underpowered null is INCONCLUSIVE, not a falsifier.

tripwires.observation: week-4 retention of activated treatment users vs control
tripwires.whatWouldFalsify: week-4 retention of the treatment cohort is at least 3pp below control (the pre-registered guardrail) — activation was bought by hurting retention. An underpowered read is inconclusive, not a pass.

stopping.giveUpCondition: return the best-argued change after 2 empty rounds
